results: Every ORIGINAL raw H1 Fourier coefficient and every shifted ORIGINAL negative endpoint norm are controlled by the SAME actual physical periodic L2 norm with constant ONE. The actual pair of resonant amplitudes has max-norm at most that physical norm, and the LITERAL original free Fourier projection has norm at most TWICE the actual amplitude max-norm.

For the ACTUAL endpoint inverse family K, BOTH signed shifted norms of K*a-a are at most TWO times the genuine source perturbation majorant times the corresponding input norm. The proof uses actual inverse uniqueness/identification and the exact identity K*a-a=T(K*a), with both opposite norm bounds already proved for the SAME inverse. Both original resonant errors of K applied to an original H1 vector are consequently bounded by TWO times the perturbation majorant times its actual physical L2 norm.

The ACTUAL reduced family is proved equal to the literal source common-diagonal complex two-by-two matrix, with the ACTUAL diagonal and ACTUAL two couplings. At an ACTUAL determinant zero its full max-pair operator action is bounded by TWO times the sum of the actual coupling norms. The common diagonal equality is proved by the existing native bilinear Green symmetry; no real-potential or diagonalizability hypothesis is imposed.

The native quantitative eta bound with source constant SIXTEEN is PROVED from the actual native eta/gamma equation, actual normalized vectors, actual free-mode one-half lower bound, actual inverse responses and actual inhomogeneous reduced equation. Its determinant-zero condition is DERIVED from the actual nonzero native eigenfunction. No effective-matrix, inverse-response or coupling-norm estimate is supplied as a hypothesis.

An explicit norm-ball cutoff makes kappa=C_r*n^(r-1/2)*norm(q)<=1/16 uniformly. Source 2.14 gives original resonant-amplitude max-norm at least1/4 for the unit eigenvector. The actual inverse changes those amplitudes by at most1/8, giving norm at least1/8 for its response; the unit second vector has response norm at most9/8. The actual reduced residual then gives norm(eta)<=9*norm(gamma)+16*(norm(b_plus)+norm(b_minus)) <=16*(norm(gamma)+norm(b_plus)+norm(b_minus)).

The source article adapter proves the constant-SIXTEEN bound for EVERY normalized original native pair satisfying the ACTUAL canonical eta equation. It therefore applies to ANY actual source normalized orthonormal spectral basis starting with its canonical lambda_n^+ eigenfunction, including coincident roots and complex associated vectors. ONE cutoff is chosen BEFORE every potential in EACH FIXED ORIGINAL complex endpoint norm ball and ALL later ORIGINAL positive indices; it can be above ANY supplied earlier cutoff.

Full source Lemma 2.13 is PROVED: the actual canonical lambda_n^+ eigenfunction and second native H1 vector have actual physical L2 norm ONE and form an ACTUAL orthonormal basis of the FULL original source-circle spectral range. BOTH vectors have IDENTICAL ENTIRE original F-ell^(s+2,infinity) distributions. The canonical eta/gamma equation AND its exact source constant16 bound with ACTUAL original couplings at the ACTUAL lambda_n^+ are proved together, uniformly on each exact original complex endpoint norm ball.
